title: The Fox and the Goat
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Fox fell into a well and was unable to get out again. By and by a thirsty Goat came by, and seeing the Fox in the well asked him if the water was good. "Good?" said the Fox, "it's the best water I ever tasted in all my life. Come down and try it yourself." The Goat thought of nothing but the prospect of quenching his thirst, and jumped in at once. When he had had enough to drink, he looked about, like the Fox, for some way of getting out, but could find none. Presently the Fox said, "I have an idea. You stand on your hind legs, and plant your forelegs firmly against the side of the well, and then I'll climb on to your back, and, from there, by stepping on your horns, I can get out. And when I'm out, I'll help you out too." The Goat did as he was requested, and the Fox climbed on to his back and so out of the well; and then he coolly walked away. The Goat called loudly after him and reminded him of his promise to help him out: but the Fox merely turned and said, "If you had as much sense in your head as you have hair in your beard you wouldn't have got into the well without making certain that you could get out again."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens to the Fox at the very start?
options: He is chased into a well by hunters
He climbs into a well to hide from a Goat
He falls into a well and cannot get out
He is pushed into a well by another fox

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Goat ask the Fox when he first arrives?
options: If the water was good
How deep the well was
How the Fox fell in
Whether the Fox was hurt

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox tell the Goat about the water?
options: That it is too cold to drink
That it is nearly gone
That it tastes strange and bitter
That it is the best water he ever tasted

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Fox's plan for getting out of the well?
options: To dig a tunnel out from the bottom
To climb on the Goat's back and then his horns
To wait until someone lowers a rope
To call loudly until a farmer hears them

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox do once he is out of the well?
options: He pulls the Goat out as promised
He goes to fetch a rope for the Goat
He coolly walks away
He apologizes for tricking the Goat

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox say about the Goat's "sense" at the end?
options: That the Goat lacks as much sense as he has hair in his beard
That the Goat is wiser than most animals in the forest
That the Goat should have jumped in sooner
That the Goat's horns are not strong enough to climb on

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Fox praise the water so highly when the Goat arrives?
options: He genuinely wants the Goat to enjoy a good drink
He is trying to warn the Goat away from danger
He hopes the Goat will bring him food afterward
He wants to lure the Goat into the well so he can use it to escape

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Goat's leap into the well reveal about his decision?
options: He knows exactly how he will escape before jumping in
He acts on his thirst without first checking whether he can get back out
He is tricked by a promise the Fox never actually makes
He jumps in only after the Fox promises him food

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Fox walked away "coolly"?
options: Quickly, as if in a panic
Sadly, feeling guilty about it
Calmly and without any shame
Loudly, boasting to every animal nearby

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: Think through the consequences before acting on a sudden urge
Goats should never trust foxes under any circumstances
Wells are more dangerous than they appear to be
It is always wise to help a stranger in trouble

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Goat want when he first comes upon the well?
options: To rest in the shade
To find the Fox some food
To warn the Fox of danger
To quench his thirst

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Goat do once he has had enough to drink?
options: He climbs straight out on his own
He looks about for some way of getting out, but finds none
He asks the Fox to leave first
He falls asleep beside the Fox

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Goat do after the Fox escapes and walks away?
options: He climbs out using the same method on his own
He refuses to speak to the Fox ever again
He calls loudly after him and reminds him of his promise
He begins digging at the bottom of the well

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Fox's plan require the Goat's cooperation in the first place?
options: The Fox needs something to stand on that he cannot reach on his own
The Fox cannot see the way out without the Goat's help
The Goat is the only one who knows the well has a bottom
The Fox promised the Goat's owner he would return safely

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Fox's final remark suggest about who is really to blame for the Goat's situation?
options: The Fox admits the trick was entirely his own fault
The Fox blames the well's owner for the whole misfortune
The Fox insists no one is at fault at all
The Fox blames the Goat's own lack of foresight, not his trick

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "prospect" mean in "the prospect of quenching his thirst"?
options: A written record of a past event
The expectation or possibility of something happening
A formal agreement between two parties
A location marked for future use

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Fox and a Goat work together and both escape the well safely
A Goat rescues a Fox and refuses any thanks in return
A Fox tricks a thirsty Goat into helping him escape, then abandons him
A Fox and a Goat argue over who fell into the well first
